text:
Kai: quick follow-up from the perf run this morning — grouped-query (GQ) beats multi-query (MQ) on short prefixes as expected, but we saw a 12% p95 regression on long-form (~8k tokens) workloads when GQ was forced by the current heuristic.
Priya: interesting, any idea if it's kernel-level or batching behavior? :thinking_face: 
Kai: looks like two things: GQ's attention kernel is doing more memory copies when KV spans pages, and our dynamic batching code isn't grouping long sequences efficiently — we end up with smaller effective batch sizes.
Oliver: can you paste the perf numbers?
Kai: sure — micro-run summary:
```
model: redwood/longform-v2
hw: A100-80GB
mode: quantized int8
workload: 8k tokens gen, batch=4
GQ (current): p95=410ms, throughput=55 tok/s
MQ (preferred fallback): p95=365ms, throughput=62 tok/s
prefix reuse < 0.2 -> GQ chosen by heuristic
```
Priya: hmmm. MQ wins on throughput+latency for long seqs. But GQ still better on small seqs right?
Kai: yes for <1k where prefix reuse >0.3. GQ still gives 20% lower CPU+GPU time there.
Zhi: my hunch: kernel selection should consider contiguous KV memory layout + seq_len distribution rather than only prefix_reuse. Right now our selector is too simplistic.
Tana: Agreed. We also need to surface whether a kernel supports strided KV accesses — that'll decide extra copy cost.
Leah: could we add a small model probe at load time that runs a few synthetic steps and reports: avg copy bytes, kernel_choice_perf_ratio, kv_stride_support? Cheap and cached per model+quantization.
Kai: exactly what I was thinking — probe would let us build per-model profiles and pick the kernel and routing policy deterministically.
Priya: API surface: are we adding this to the model manifest (static) or to the runtime profile cache (mutable)? 
Zhi: runtime profile cache. Manifests are heavy to churn. Probes can run once per pinned model variant on first warmup and be invalidated on quantization changes.
Oliver: fallback ordering idea: prefer kernel with lower expected p95 for the 90th percentile sequence length for that deployment (we already collect seq_len histograms). If memory copy overhead exceeds threshold, choose MQ.
Tana: threshold should be stored as a tunable with safe defaults. Also include a cap: never pick GQ if estimated KV copy > 1GB per request unless customer pin overrides.
Leah: can someone sketch the new selector proto? I can add tests to perf harness.
Kai: rough config/snippet for selector heuristics: 
```
kernel_selector:
  probes_enabled: true
  metrics_collected: [p95, throughput, kv_copy_bytes]
  policy:
    - if seq_len_p90 < 1024 and prefix_reuse > 0.25 -> prefer: GQ
    - else if kv_copy_bytes_est > 1e9 -> prefer: MQ
    - else compare: expected_p95_est -> prefer lower
  fallback_order: [preferred, alternate]
```
Priya: love the simplicity. Need to decide where expected_p95_est comes from — historical telemetry vs probe extrapolation?
Zhi: probe + lightweight model regression is best. Telemetry is noisy across tenants/hardware. Probe on the same instance/hw gives more accurate kernel-level costs.
Oliver: operational concern: probes add startup latency. How long are they?
Kai: 3-5 synthetic steps takes ~200-400ms on warm GPUs. We can run them async and use conservative defaults until probe completes.
Leah: I'll add a test to the nightly perf job to validate that probe+selector picks MQ for the longform config above and GQ for shortform.
Tana: also add a fallback circuit: if chosen kernel shows >10% regressing vs baseline in live ops for 5 minutes, auto-fallback and mark for investigation.
Priya: what about the interface boundary — should scheduler call kernel_selector or kernel_selector call scheduler with hints?
Zhi: keep kernel_selector pure (stateless) given model profile + request hints, return one of: {kernel_name, reason, expected_costs}. Scheduler consumes that and decides batching/placement. Keeps separation of concerns.
Oliver: agree. Also add a lightweight contract: selector must be idempotent and cheap (<100us) after probe to avoid adding overhead in hot path.
Kai: next steps I propose: 1) Leah adds probe harness + model profile store (LRU cache keyed by model+quant) 2) Zhi implements selector algo with the policy snippet 3) Tana adds fallback circuit + alerting 4) Priya/Oliver wire scheduler to accept selector hints.
Priya: timeline?
Leah: I can have probe harness + perf test in 4 days.
Zhi: selector PR in 1 week after that.
Tana: fallback circuit + docs 1 week.
Kai: ok. one more: please capture this as a short RFC follow-up (design + config example + probe cost). I'll draft and tag reviewers.
infra-bot: canary-deploy finished for runtime-runtime-a  (deploy id: dpl-2026-0319-8) :white_check_mark:
Priya: awesome, thanks. I'll watch the perf dashboard tonight for any deviation. :eyes:
Oliver: thanks everyone — lean and pragmatic. We'll iterate once we have probe telemetry.
Kai: thanks — I'll post the RFC link when drafted.
